Law as an institution is lifeworld law: particular norms, such as constitutional basics and the moral core of criminal law, still need moral-practical justification and give binding form to shared communicative expectations. Law as a medium is positivized steering law that organizes markets and administration, drawing legitimacy from the legal order as a whole and carrying systemic imperatives into everyday spheres such as family, school, and social life. No answer choices were attached, so this is the distinction itself.

CONFIDENCE: 86
